title: Corey Haines on running a SaaS portfolio, AEO, and why harder markets are better
summary: Corey Haines explains how a marketer-turned-builder runs services, products and a personal brand as one portfolio. He covers the order of marketing channels, how AEO works in practice, and why picking harder, niche problems creates a moat.

principles.text: Run services, products and a personal brand as one portfolio so each supports the others.
principles.quote: I can have like my personal media business and then I can have my services business conversion factory which is cash flowing and a nice job. And then I can have my products which are more like my moonshots

principles.text: Keep adding projects only if each one trends up or plateaus; avoid a treadmill of products that spike then decline.
principles.quote: the numbers should kind of always be going up or at least plateau. Why would I keep making more things that go up and then go down? I I don't want to play that game personally.

principles.text: Stack marketing channels in order (SEO/AEO, Google Ads, Meta, and so on) and stop when you hit resistance.
principles.quote: I'm always going to start with SEO, and now that's basically AEO, too. And then I'm going to move on to Google Ads

principles.text: Good AEO is good SEO plus good product marketing plus a broad brand footprint of web mentions.
principles.quote: good AEO is first of all good SEO. So, just check that box.

principles.text: AI visibility work can unlock pent-up demand; one niche client doubled traffic and tripled booked calls in three months.
principles.quote: their traffic doubled in 3 months and their booked calls tripled in 3 months.

principles.text: Pick the harder thing, whether a product or a marketing channel, because the barrier to entry protects you.
principles.quote: the harder it is, the better because that means that it's just higher barrier of entry for other people.
